how should I know? phrase

also how would I know?, how am I supposed to know?, how do I know?

classical

Ter. And. 791: Eho inepta, nescīs quid sit āctum? — Quī sciam?

Quī sciam?

quī, the old ablative “how”, with the deliberative subjunctive

The comic retort: a slave-girl, asked whether she doesn’t know what has happened. Quī here is the adverb “how”, not the relative.

Other words

  • Quōmodo sciam? — how should I know?

    deliberative subjunctive: “how am I to know?” · also used · modern · Traupman 35: how should I know?, quōmodo sciam?

    Traupman’s question. The subjunctive makes it a protest, as in Quid faciam?, what am I to do? Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

Examples

  • Ubi sunt calceī meī? — Quōmodo sciam?

    Where are my shoes? — How should I know?Traupman 35

  • Eho inepta, nescīs quid sit āctum? — Quī sciam?

    Hey, silly, don’t you know what’s happened? — How should I know?Ter. And. 791

See also know, what am I to do?.

SourcesLewis & Short: scio

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 35.
